Rashi on Ketubot 31b:12:1.english: These are those who are flogged - If they warned them.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:1:1.hebrew: פטור - מתשלומין, דאתי עליה חיוב שבת מחמת הגבהה ראשונה שבה נקנה לו הכיס, ומיתה ותשלומין באין כאחד:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:1:1.english: Exempt - From payment, for liability for [violating] Shabbat comes upon him because of the initial lifting, through which the purse was acquired by him, and [thus] death and payment come as one.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:1:2.hebrew: ניפלוג בדידה - במגביה עצמו, יכול לשנות בו חיוב ופטור:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:1:2.english: Let [him] distinguish within it itself - In [the case of] lifting itself, [he] can teach in it [both] liability and exemption.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:1.hebrew: אלא - לא תוקמה כשעמד, ואפ"ה חיוב שבת דעקירה לאו מחמת עקירה ראשונה דהגבהה אתיא ליה, אלא בעקירת גופו של פסיעה אחרונה כשיוצא מן הבית, ובן עזאי היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:1.english: Rather - Do not establish it [as referring to a case] where he stopped, and even so, the Shabbat liability for lifting does not come to him on account of the first lifting of picking [it] up, but rather through the lifting of his body [in] the final step when he exits the house, and it is [the opinion of] Ben Azzai:

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:2.english: Who said - In the first chapter of [Tractate] Shabbat.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:3.hebrew: מהלך כעומד דמי - ועקירת כל פסיעה הויא עקירה, והנחת הרגל היא הנחה. הלכך, קניה משעת הגבהה, וחיוב מיתה בפסיעה בתרייתא קא אתיא ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:3.english: One who walks is like one who stands - And the lifting [of the foot] at each step is a [halakhic] lifting, and the placing down of the foot is a [halakhic] placement. Therefore, he acquires it from the moment of lifting [it], and the liability for the death penalty comes to him at the final step.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:4.english: But [if] one throws, what [is the halakha] - He lifted it and threw it.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:5.hebrew: פטור - מתשלומין, דאתיא ליה חיוב שבת ע"י חיוב הגבהה, דתו ליתא עקירה אחריתי:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:2:5.english: Exempt - from payment, since Shabbat liability comes to him through the liability [incurred by] lifting, as there is no other lifting.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:3:1.english: This is not a manner of carrying out - And there is no Shabbat liability here.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:4:1.english: And in what [case] - was it necessary to teach us that this is the manner of carrying out?

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:4:2.english: If [it is] with large [purses] - A large purse that has a load [too heavy] to lift it.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:4:3.hebrew: אורחיה הוא - לגררו, ופשיטא דהוצאה היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:4:3.english: It is its manner - to drag it, and it is obvious that it is [an act of] carrying out.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:4:4.english: It is not its manner - And why is he liable on account of Shabbat?

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:1.hebrew: איסור גניבה ליכא - דמשיכה בלא הגבהה קס"ד דלא קניא ברה"ר:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:1.english: There is no prohibition of theft - For we initially assumed that pulling [an object] without lifting [it] does not acquire in the public domain.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:2.hebrew: לרשות היחיד - לרשותו, שהיתה חצירו סמוכה לחצר הבעלים:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:2.english: To a private domain - To his [own] domain, for his courtyard was adjacent to the owner's courtyard.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:3.hebrew: צידי רה"ר - סמוך לבתים, שנותנין להלן מן הבתים אבנים ומכשולין להרחיק חיכוך העגלות, ומאותן חיפופי ולפנים קרי צידי רה"ר:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:5:3.english: The sides of the public domain - [The area] adjacent to the houses, where they place stones and barriers beyond the houses to keep away the scraping of wagons; and from those protective barriers inward is called the sides of the public domain.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:6:1.english: The dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis [is] in Eruvin, in the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:7:1.english: For the public is not [typically] found [there] - And [therefore] it is like a simta [a side alley], in which [the Sages] instituted [acquisition by] meshikhah [pulling].

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - מגרר ויוצא דקאמר פטור, לעולם ברשות הרבים, ודקשיא לך איסור גניבה ליכא:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:1.english: Rav Ashi said - [Regarding] "one who drags [it] and goes out," where [it] says he is exempt, [it is] actually in the public domain; and as for what was difficult for you, [that] there is no prohibition of theft:

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:2.hebrew: כגון שצירף ידו - השניה לפחות משלשה סמוך לקרקע, ובידו אחת גיררה ונפלה לתוך חברתה, וידו קניא ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:2.english: Where he joined his hand - [that is,] his other [hand] at less than three [handbreadths], close to the ground, and with his one hand he dragged it and it fell into the other [hand], and his hand acquires [it] for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:3.hebrew: כדרבא דאמר רבא ידו של אדם חשובה - לענין הנחת שבת, כמקום ארבעה על ארבעה. וכי היכי דלענין שבת חשוב מקום, לענין מיקנא נמי חשוב מקום למיקני, כאילו הגביהה למעלה משלשה. ומיהו, ברשות היחיד לא אגבהה דתיקני ליה מקמי דליתי חיוב שבת עליה, וביאתה לרה"ר וקנייתה באין כאחד. ולהכי משני כשצירף, דלא תיהוי הגבהה ברשות היחיד, כדקתני מגרר ויוצא:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:3.english: In accordance with Rava, as Rava said: A person's hand is considered - With respect to placing [an object] on Shabbat, [it is considered] like a place of four by four [handbreadths]. And just as with respect to Shabbat it is considered a [significant] place, with respect to acquiring [an object] it is also considered a [significant] place to acquire [it], as though he lifted it above three [handbreadths]. However, in the private domain he did not lift it such that he would acquire it before the Shabbat liability comes upon him, and [thus] its entry into the public domain and his acquisition of it come simultaneously. And for this reason [Rav Ashi] answers [that it is a case] where he joined [his hand], so that there should not be lifting in the private domain, as it teaches: "he drags [it] and goes out."

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:4.hebrew: רב אחא מתני הכי - כדאמרן, דמשיכה ברשות הרבים לא קני, ומוקים לה כשצירף ידו וקיבלה לתוכה:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:8:4.english: Rav Acha taught thus - As we have said, that pulling [an object] in the public domain does not effect acquisition, and he establishes it [in a case] where he joined his hand and received it inside [his hand].

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:1.hebrew: היה מושכו - בגונב בהמה ברשות בעלים קאי, בפרק מרובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:1.english: He was pulling it - [It] refers to one who steals an animal in the owner's domain, in the chapter [entitled] Merubeh.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:3.hebrew: ברשות הבעלים פטור - הגנב מלשלם כלום, דלא קני להתחייב באונסין:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:3.english: In the domain of the owner, [he is] exempt - The thief [is exempt] from paying anything, because he did not acquire [it] to become liable for unavoidable accidents.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:4.english: He lifted it - Even in the owner's domain.

Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:5.hebrew: הא הוציאו - כל היכא דאפקיה, ואפי' לרה"ר:
Rashi on Ketubot 31b:9:5.english: Thus, [if] he took it out - wherever he took it out, even to the public domain.

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:12:1.hebrew: ורמינהי אלו הן הלוקין הבא על אחותו - ארישא דמתניתין הוה מצי למיפרך, דקתני "הבא על הממזרת יש לה קנס", והתם קתני דלקי עלה; אלא נטר הכא עד "הבא על אחותו" למיפרך מרישא דמתניתין דהתם, דחייבי לאוין שנויין שם בתר חייבי כריתות, והיה צריך להביא כל המשנה עד "הבא על הממזרת":
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:12:1.english: And they raised a contradiction: "These are the ones who are flogged: One who has relations with his sister..." - [The Gemara] could have raised the objection against the beginning of our Mishnah, which teaches: "One who has relations with a mamzeret, she receives a fine," whereas there [in Makkot] it teaches that one is flogged for [relations with] her. Rather, it waited here until "One who has relations with his sister" in order to raise the objection from the beginning of the Mishnah there, because those liable to negative commandments are taught there after those liable to karet, and [otherwise] it would have had to cite the entire Mishnah up to "One who has relations with a mamzeret."

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:2:1.hebrew: מהלך כעומד דמי - ומעביר ארבע אמות דחייב ברה"ר, הלכתא גמירי לה כדאמרינן בהזורק (שבת דף צו:), ולא ילפינן מינה, דהתם מקום חיובא הוא, אבל בן עזאי מיירי במהלך מחנות לפלטיא דרך סטיו שהוא מקום פטור. ובירושלמי פריך: לבן עזאי היכי משכחת מעביר ד"א ברה"ר דמיחייב? ומשני: בקופץ:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:2:1.english: One who walks is like one who stands - And [the law of] one who carries [an object] four cubits, that he is liable in a public domain, is a received tradition, as we say in [the chapter] HaZorek (Shabbat 96b), and we do not derive from it [for our case], for there it is a place of liability, whereas Ben Azzai is speaking of one who walks from a store to a plaza via a colonnade, which is an exempt area. And in the Yerushalmi it asks: According to Ben Azzai, how can you find [a case of] one who carries [an object] four cubits in a public domain where he is liable? And it answers: Where he jumps.

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:2:2.hebrew: אבל זורק מאי — פטור? ליפלוג וליתני בדידה - משום הכי חשיב זורק בדידה טפי ממגרר, משום דבמוציא ובזורק — בשניהם בא בהגבהה הקנין קודם שיבא חיוב הוצאה; אבל במגרר, ההוצאה והקנין באין כאחד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:2:2.english: "But [if] one throws, what [is the law]? He is exempt! Let [the Tanna] distinguish and teach within [the case] itself." - For this reason [the Gemara] considers throwing [to be] "within [the case] itself" more than dragging, because in [the case of] one who carries out and in [the case of] one who throws, in both of them the acquisition comes through lifting before the liability for carrying out arrives; whereas in [the case of] one who drags, the carrying out and the acquisition come simultaneously.

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:3:1.hebrew: מגרר ויוצא איצטריך ליה - לעיל דפריך דליפלוג בין לפוש ובין לכתף, לא בעי לשנויי הכי, משום דלכתף פטור נראה לו חידוש טפי מחידוש דמגרר. [ועוד, דהכא לא הוי לגמרי בדידה, אבל לעיל דהוי ממש בדידה — לא שייך לשנויי הכי]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:3:1.english: "Dragging and exiting was necessary for him" - Earlier, when [the Gemara] asked that [the Mishnah] should distinguish between [stopping] to rest and [stopping] to shoulder [the burden], it did not want to answer thus, because [the rule] that [stopping] to shoulder [the burden] is exempt appeared to it [to be] a greater novelty than the novelty of dragging. [And furthermore, here it is not entirely within the same case, whereas earlier, where it is literally within the same case, it is not appropriate to answer thus.]

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:4:1.hebrew: אלא במיצעי - תימה לר"י, דבפרק הספינה (ב"ב דף פו. ושם), גבי "דברים שדרכן להגביהן אין נקנין במשיכה אלא בהגבהה", ופריך מהגונב כיס: דבר הגבהה הוא! ומשני: במידי דבעי מיתנא. משמע דאי הוה אמר "דבר הגבהה נמי נקנה במשיכה", הוה אתי ליה שפיר אפילו בזוטרי. ואמאי? הא על כרחך לא מצי איירי בזוטרי, דא"כ היכי מיחייב לענין שבת בגרירה, דאין דרך הוצאה בכך? וי"ל: דאפשר שיהא דרך הוצאה בכך אפילו בזוטרי, כגון שמוציאו דרך מחתרת, דדרכו בגרירה ואינו נקנה אלא בהגבהה. אי נמי: הוה מצי למימר "ולטעמיך", ולא פריך; וכן דרך הש"ס בכמה מקומות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:4:1.english: "Rather, [it refers] to intermediate[-sized purses]" - It is astonishing to Ri, for in the chapter [entitled] HaSefinah (Bava Batra 86a and there), regarding [the principle that] items whose way is to be lifted are not acquired through pulling, only through lifting, [the Gemara] asks from [the baraita of] "one who steals a purse [on Shabbat]": [surely] it is an item of lifting! And [the Gemara] answers: [It refers] to something that requires a rope [to be dragged]. This implies that if it had said [that] an item of lifting is also acquired through pulling, it would have worked out well for it even with small [purses]. But why? Surely, perforce, [the baraita] cannot be speaking of small [purses], for if so, how would one be liable with respect to Shabbat for dragging [it], since that is not the normal manner of carrying out? And one can answer that it is possible for that to be a normal manner of carrying out even with small [purses], for example, when one takes it out through a tunnel, where its normal manner is by dragging, yet it is acquired only through lifting. Alternatively, [the Gemara there] could have said "And according to your reasoning..." [to raise this objection], but it did not ask [it]; and such is the way of the Talmud in several places.

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:5:1.hebrew: אי דאפקיה לרה"ר איסור גניבה ליכא - אף על גב דאיכא למ"ד בפ"ק דב"מ (דף י. ושם) דד' אמות קונות לו לאדם אפילו ברה"ר, ה"מ גבי מציאה — דלא ליתו לאינצויי, ובגט — משום עיגונא; אבל לגנב לא תקינו שיקנו לו ד' אמות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:5:1.english: If he carried it out to the public domain, there is no prohibition [against] theft - Even though there is [an opinion] that says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (10a and ad loc.) that a person's four cubits acquire [an item] for him even in the public domain, that applies [only] regarding a lost object, so that [people] will not come to quarrel, and regarding a bill of divorce, because of [the concern of] igun; however, for a thief, [the Sages] did not institute that [his] four cubits should acquire [an item] for him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:8:1.hebrew: רב אשי אמר כגון שצירף ידו למטה מג' וקיבלה וכדרבא - פירש בקונטרס דקאי אמאי דפריך לעיל: איסור גניבה ליכא, והשתא משני דאיכא נמי איסור גניבה, כדרבא. וקשה לר"י: חדא, דמה ענין חשיבות מקום ד' דלענין שבת לקנין? ועוד, דאין צריך שום ראיה להביא דקניא ליה ידו, דפשיטא ד"ונתן בידה" אמר רחמנא, כדפרישית לעיל. ועוד, דאמאי לא מוקי אפילו כשצירף ידו למעלה מג', כגון שהאסקופה גבוהה ג', דליכא הגבהה ברה"י, והוה מייתי מדרבא אקנין ואשבת? ונראה כגירסת הספר שמצא ר"י בן רבינו מאיר בספרי אשכנז, דגרס: "אי נמי כדרבא". וכולה מילתא אשבת קאי: כשצירף ידו למטה מג' — דאע"ג דלא חשיבא לענין שבת הנחה אלא על גבי מקום ד', איכא הכא חיוב שבת כשצירף ידו למטה מג', דלמטה מג' לא בעינן מקום ד', דכלבוד דמי וכמונחת אארעא דמיא; אי נמי אפי' צירף ידו למעלה מג', וכדרבא, דידו חשובה כד' על ד'. ור"ת ל"ג: "דאמר רבא ידו של אדם", אלא "וכדרבא" ותו לא. ואתא לשנויי ד"מגרר ויוצא" איצטריך ליה לאשמועינן דאגד יד לא שמיה אגד, ואהא מייתי כדרבא דאמר בהמצניע (שבת דף צב.) דאגד יד לא שמיה אגד. ומיירי כשהוא נשאר בפנים והוציא ידו אחת ובאחרת מגרר לתוכה; ודוקא צירף למטה מג', דלמעלה משלשה שמיה אגד, דבתר גופו גרירא. [ולפי' קמא קשה, דלשנויא קמא לית ליה דרבא, וכולהו מתנייתא דשבת וכן ר' יוחנן (שבת ה.) אתו כרבא]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:8:1.english: Rav Ashi said: [It is] a case where he joined his hand below three [handbreadths] and received it; and in accordance with Rava - Rashi explained that this refers to what [the Gemara] asked earlier: "Is there no prohibition of theft?!" And now [Rav Ashi] answers that there is also a prohibition of theft, in accordance with Rava. And this is difficult for Ri: First, what connection does the significance of a place of four [by four handbreadths] with regard to Shabbat have to acquisition? And furthermore, there is no need to bring any proof that his hand acquires for him, for it is obvious, as the Merciful One said, "and he shall put it in her hand" (Deuteronomy 24:1), as I explained above. And furthermore, why does [Rav Ashi] not establish [the case] even when he joined his hand above three [handbreadths], such as where the threshold is three [handbreadths] high, so that there is no lifting in the private domain, and he would [then] bring [proof] from Rava both for acquisition and for Shabbat? Rather, it appears [correct] like the reading of the book that R. Yitzchak ben Rabbenu Meir found in the manuscripts of Ashkenaz, which reads: "Alternatively, [it is] in accordance with Rava." And the entire matter refers to Shabbat: When he joined his hand below three [handbreadths] — even though with regard to Shabbat, placement is not considered [valid] except on a place of four [by four handbreadths], here there is Shabbat liability when he joined his hand below three [handbreadths], because below three [handbreadths] we do not require a place of four [by four handbreadths], for it is like lavud [legally attached] and is considered as resting on the ground; alternatively, even if he joined his hand above three [handbreadths], [he is liable] in accordance with Rava, for his hand is considered like four by four [handbreadths]. And Rabbeinu Tam does not read [the text]: "for Rava said: A person's hand," rather [he reads] "and in accordance with Rava" and nothing more. And [Rav Ashi] comes to answer that "dragging and exiting" was needed to teach us that the containment of a hand (eged yad) is not considered a binding (eged), and regarding this he brings [the statement] in accordance with Rava, who said in [chapter] Hamatzni'a (Shabbat 92a) that the containment of a hand is not considered a binding. And it is speaking of a case where he remains inside [the private domain] and extended one hand [into the public domain], and with the other [hand] he drags [the object] into it; and specifically [when] he joined [his hand] below three [handbreadths], for above three [handbreadths] it is considered a binding, since it is drawn after his body. [And according to the first explanation it is difficult, for according to the first answer [the Gemara] does not hold of Rava, whereas all the Mishnahs of Shabbat and likewise R. Yochanan (Shabbat 5a) accord with Rava.]

Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:9:1.hebrew: וברשות הרבים נמי קנה - והא דאמר בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב פד:), דאביי ורבא דאמרי תרוייהו דמשיכה לא קניא ברה"ר — אומר ר"י דלא פליגי אדרבינא דהכא, דהא דקאמר דקני היינו לענין להתחייב באונסין, אבל אינו קונה שיהא שלו לגמרי. וריצב"א נראה לו דפליג, דהא במרובה (ב"ק דף עט. ושם) גבי "נתנה לבכורות בנו" דקתני סיפא, איכא נמי למידק כמו שמדקדק כאן, והתם לענין משיכה דקנין איירי ללשון ראשון שפי' שם בקונט'; ואפילו ללשון שני, הא מוכח התם בגמ' (דף סה.) שאין לגנב להתחייב אלא במשיכה הראויה לקנין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 31b:9:1.english: "And in the public domain he also acquires [it]" - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in [Chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 84b), where Abaye and Rava both say that pulling (meshikhah) does not acquire in a public domain — Rabbi Yitzchak says that they do not disagree with Ravina here, for that which [Ravina] says that he acquires [it] is [only] with respect to becoming liable for unavoidable accidents, but he does not acquire [it] such that it becomes completely his. And to Rabbi Yitzchak ben Avraham (Ritsba) it appears that they do disagree, for in [Chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 79a and there [onward]), regarding [the case of] "he gave it for his son's firstborn [redemption]" that the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches, one can also make the [same] inference as [Ravina] infers here; and there it is dealing with pulling that effects acquisition according to the first explanation that Rashi (Kuntres) explained there; and even according to the second explanation, it is proven there in the Gemara (65a) that a thief does not become liable except through pulling that is valid for acquisition.
